post.title: They Can't See Your Nerves #shorts
post.description: Sam is sure the whole room can see his shaking hands. Research says they can't, at least not as much as he thinks. Gilovich, Savitsky & Medvec (1998) called it the illusion of transparency: we overestimate how readable our inner states are. In Savitsky & Gilovich (2003, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology), students gave impromptu speeches; speakers thought they looked more nervous than observers saw, and speakers who were told about the illusion beforehand gave talks that observers rated better and more composed (simple reassurance didn't help). #psychology #shorts #publicspeaking #anxiety
